n: The father now speaks to all his children, inviting them to pay attention so they can gain understanding.
He assures them his teaching is good and worth holding onto. A parent’s instruction is offered as a gift, not a burden.

f.g: doctrine = teaching, what is received by learning.

n: The father remembers his own childhood: he too was once a tender, cherished son. If Solomon is the speaker, this recalls David and Bathsheba, though the passage could fit any father.

f.g: Young, delicate, and especially dear—“only” can mean uniquely loved.

n: He quotes what his father taught him. Wisdom is passed down generation to generation—each parent teaching what they themselves received.
The grandfather’s words continue: acquire wisdom and understanding, and never drift away from them.

f.g: “Get” means acquire or buy, as in a purchase.

n: Wisdom is pictured as a faithful companion who will guard you if you stay loyal to her and love her.
Wisdom is the most important thing. Whatever it costs, even all you have, get understanding.

f.g: Or “The beginning of wisdom is: get wisdom!”
With all you possess—spend everything if needed.

n: If you prize wisdom highly, she will raise you up and bring you honor when you hold her close.
Wisdom crowns the one who loves her with a beautiful wreath and a crown of glory.
The father returns to his own voice: listen, and you will have a long life.

f.w: the years of thy life shall be many

n: He has guided his son in the straight paths of wisdom—now the son must keep walking in them.
On the path of wisdom, you have room to move and can even run without tripping.
Grip instruction tightly and never let it go, because it is your very life.
Don’t even step onto the road of the wicked.

f.w: Enter not into the path of the wicked

n: Four quick commands pile up for emphasis: avoid it, don’t go near it, turn away, keep moving. The best way to resist temptation is distance.
The wicked are so addicted to doing harm that they can’t sleep until they’ve caused someone to fall.

f.g: mischief = harm, evil (stronger than the modern meaning).

n: Wickedness and violence are their daily bread and wine. What they live on is what they become.

f.g: Food gained by wickedness, or wickedness as their constant diet.

n: A beautiful image: the life of the righteous is like dawn, growing brighter and brighter until full noon. Spiritual growth is gradual and increasing.
The wicked walk in deep darkness and don’t even know what makes them stumble.

f.w: they know not at what they stumble

n: A new lesson begins with the familiar call to listen carefully.
Keep these words both in sight and deep in your heart.

f.w: keep them in the midst of thine heart

n: Wise words bring life and health to the whole body. Spiritual wholeness and physical well-being are connected in Proverbs.
Guard your heart above all else, because everything in your life flows out of it. In Hebrew, the heart is the center of thoughts, desires, and choices.

f.w: Keep thy heart with all diligence

n: After the heart, the mouth: get rid of twisted, dishonest speech.
Next, the eyes: look straight ahead and keep your focus on the goal, not on distractions.
Then the feet: think carefully about where you are walking, and your path will be steady.
Don’t swerve right or left; keep your foot away from evil. Heart, mouth, eyes, and feet—the whole person must stay on the path.

f.w: Turn not to the right hand nor to the left
